But the entry verified only a subset of what actually reaches the model. _build_messages (processor.py:181) builds the outbound prompt via `_render_template(self.config.prompt_template, input_text, fields)`, and _render_template (processor.py:56-68) substitutes every other CSV column / JSONL field into `{column}` placeholders — this is BatchLLM's own headlined "Multi-field templates" feature (README:43, 171-181; e.g. `-t "Translate this review to {language}, then summarize it in one line: {text}"`), not an obscure edge case. `fields` is absent from `_make_checkpoint_fingerprint`'s hash (processor.py:307-320, which hashes only items/model/system_prompt/prompt_template/max_tokens/temperature/base_url/max_retries/timeout), is never persisted to the checkpoint file at all (`_save_checkpoint`, processor.py:399-421, writes only index/input/output/error/error_type/tokens_in/tokens_out/latency_ms), and is not covered by the per-row load check (processor.py:343 compares only `data.get("input","") != items[idx]`, i.e. the raw input-column text, never the rendered prompt). Concrete failure: checkpoint a multi-field run, interrupt it, edit only the `language` (or any non-input) column for an already-completed row, resume with the same `--checkpoint` — fingerprint matches, per-row input matches, and the stale translation is replayed verbatim; the row the model would actually read on a fresh call is never sent. This is structurally the same defect this same register already downgraded at id 259 (bespokelabs/curator, sweep-14): a hash over a declared subset of the generative inputs ("recipe") rather than the full rendered request, with an untracked remainder free to drift the real outbound content while the guard reports a clean match. BatchLLM's case is if anything more clear-cut than curator's — id 259 needed a non-pure-function hypothesis to trigger; this needs only normal use of a documented, first-class feature plus a checkpoint resume. The submitted entry's own "trap" section caught the narrower api_key exclusion but missed this larger, code-confirmed gap entirely. Per the id 259 precedent in this register, a fingerprint/replay guard that verifiably checks a proxy for the request rather than the request's actual content does not meet PASS_REPLAY's bar — downgrading PASS_REPLAY -> FAIL.

name: Fast mode (Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8): confirmed 2x price multiplier; the same-weights claim is a documentation sentence and caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY
reasoning: Quote verified verbatim on live fetch: 'Fast mode runs the same model with a faster inference configuration. There is no change to intelligence or capabilities' — and separately, the bullet 'Same model weights and behavior (not a different model).' Pricing confirmed against the live pricing page's model table: Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 standard is $5/MTok input, $25/MTok output; fast-mode pricing (same fast-mode page and pricing page agree) is $10/MTok input, $50/MTok output — exactly a 2x multiplier on both legs. Also confirmed: 'Fast mode pricing stacks with other pricing modifiers: Prompt caching multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing / Data residency multipliers apply on top of fast mode pricing' (verbatim on both pages). Per the bar, this same-weights assertion is Anthropic's own word about its own inference stack — however unambiguous the phrasing, a documentation sentence never supports more than CONTRACTUAL_ONLY. A structural wrinkle on the same page cuts the other way from a harmless assumption: 'Switching between fast and standard speed invalidates the prompt cache. Requests at different speeds do not share cached prefixes' — meaning fast and standard demonstrably run through disjoint cache/serving infrastructure, corroborating (without proving) that the underlying path differs enough that an identity claim needs independent verification, not just trust. On the miner's cross-reference: this candidate claims to correct 'the register's own entry 87 framing.' Entry 87, as it currently stands (docs/research/2026-08-10-verdicts-final.json), is OpenAI's service_tier=priority|fast — a different provider, different field, different product, already INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE for an unrelated reason (its own cited OpenAI pages 404'd). There is nothing to correct under id 87. What this candidate actually resolves is entry 78's open sub-claim on Anthropic Fast Mode ('no vendor statement guaranteeing fast-mode output is identical to standard-mode output for the same prompt' — INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE): that vendor statement now exists verbatim, and per the bar it resolves 78's identity question to CONTRACTUAL_ONLY, not further.
savings: None — Fast mode is a documented +100% premium on both input and output tokens for Opus 5/4.8 ($5/$25 to $10/$50 per MTok), purchasing throughput rather than reducing cost.

name: Spend Limits API: per-Claude-Enterprise-member spend-limit hierarchy and increase-request workflow, structurally distinct from org/workspace tier caps (entry 126) — enforcement mechanic unconfirmed
reasoning: Verified verbatim on live fetch: 'The Spend Limits API lets you set a spend limit on each Claude Enterprise member, see where each member's spend limit is inherited from, and review or act on members' requests for a higher limit.' Confirmed structurally: 8 endpoints across two resources (spend limits: list-effective/retrieve/create/delete; increase requests: list/retrieve/approve/deny); a `source` field on each member's effective row taking values `user` (per-user override) > `seat_tier` > `rbac_group` > `organization` fallback; `amount` nullable, where `null` = unlimited and `"0"` = 'the member cannot use Claude beyond their plan's included usage' (verbatim); and a member-initiated request → admin approve/deny workflow, gated on Claude Enterprise plus 'usage credits' being enabled. This is genuinely distinct from the register's existing id 126 (org/workspace Start/Build/Scale tier caps, $500/$1,000/$200,000): per-member rather than per-org, resolved from a scope hierarchy rather than a flat tier table, and carrying an approval-request workflow 126 has no analog for. Where this candidate overreaches: it frames itself as a clean parallel to 126's PASS_ABSOLUTE. But 126's PASS_ABSOLUTE rested on an explicit operational sentence — 'Once you reach your tier's spend cap, API usage pauses until the next month' — which grounded a structural binary-gate argument (itself contested twice in this register's own corrections log, including a 2026-08-18 finding that a separate audit got zero hits on 126's quoted string on the same page). This page states only what `amount:"0"` means conceptually ('cannot use Claude beyond... included usage'), not what happens operationally when a nonzero per-member cap is reached mid-period — block, throttle, or a claude.ai-UI-only gate that leaves the raw API untouched are all consistent with that sentence. I looked for the companion page that might settle it: platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-credits and .../manage-claude/spend-limits both 404'd on 2026-08-20. Without that anchor sentence, I'm not extending 126's structural argument here — this stays a documentation-sourced description of a governance API's shape, which caps at CONTRACTUAL_ONLY.
savings: None — a governance/spend-visibility API (per-member read + override + approval workflow), not a token-cost-reduction mechanism. Value is limiting overspend, the same framing id 126 uses for its org-level analog.
provenance: Primary source re-fetched during adjudication (2026-08-20): platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api fetched live in full. Endpoint table, hierarchy/`source` field description, and `amount` semantics all confirmed verbatim. Attempted platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/usage-credits and .../manage-claude/spend-limits to find an explicit enforcement-mechanic sentence; both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-20.
telemetrySignal: `GET /v1/organizations/spend_limits/effective` is a pure metadata read — returns each member's `amount`, `source`, and `period_to_date_spend` without touching any Messages API request. An audit can build a full spend-limit inventory and a near-limit alert entirely from this endpoint with zero request-content involvement.
verifiedAgainst: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/spend-limits-api, fetched 2026-08-20 (two companion pages checked and 404'd, same date).
trap: Reading 'spend limit' and assuming it behaves exactly like the org-level hard cap (id 126) is the untested assumption this entry exists to flag: they are different products (Enterprise per-member allowance vs. org/workspace tier cap), documented on different pages, and only one of the two has a primary-source sentence describing what happens at the boundary.
settlingExperiment: Set a per-user spend-limit override via `POST /v1/organizations/spend_limits` at an amount just above a test Enterprise member's current `period_to_date_spend`, then send a Messages API call authenticated as that member once spend crosses it, and observe the literal response: a blocked/error response (matches id 126's binary-gate precedent, promotes this to PASS_ABSOLUTE) versus anything else (degraded, warned-but-allowed, or a claude.ai-surface-only block that leaves the raw API unaffected).
